punchline: The word scrum came from a 1986 paper that compared product teams to rugby, long before it named a software method.
thirty_sec: In 1986 two professors, Takeuchi and Nonaka, studied car, copier and printer firms and compared their teams to rugby, passing the ball back and forth. In the early 1990s Jeff Sutherland, who had flown reconnaissance missions as a pilot, used a similar approach at Easel and called it scrum. In 1995 he and Ken Schwaber presented it in a paper.
